items.jp: すしって何ですか

translation.pt-BR: O que é sushi?
translation.en: What is sushi?

items.label: interrogative particle
items.explanation: か at the end turns the sentence into a question.

items.jp: もう時間がないじゃないか

translation.pt-BR: Já não temos mais tempo, viu?
translation.en: We don't have any more time, you know.

items.label: emphatic/confirmatory sentence-final particle
items.explanation: か closes the expression 〜じゃないか, giving the tone of 'isn't that so?' / 'see?', insisting that the other acknowledge the fact.

items.jp: あした 行くか 行かないか まだ わかりません

translation.pt-BR: Ainda não sei se vou amanhã ou não.
translation.en: I still don't know whether I'll go tomorrow or not.

items.label: alternative particle (whether... or)
items.explanation: This か marks 行く (I go) as the first alternative of the indirect question 'whether I go or not'.

items.jp: あした 行くか 行かないか まだ わかりません

translation.pt-BR: Ainda não sei se vou amanhã ou não.
translation.en: I still don't know whether I'll go tomorrow or not.

items.label: alternative particle (whether... or)
items.explanation: This second か marks 行かない (I do not go) as the opposite alternative, closing the construction か～か within the indirect question.

items.jp: もしもし、今話せますか

translation.pt-BR: Alô, você pode falar agora?
translation.en: Hello, can you talk right now?

items.label: interrogative particle
items.explanation: The か at the end turns the statement into a question. Here it turns 話せます ('can speak') into the polite question 'can you speak?'.

items.jp: どこかで会いましたか

translation.pt-BR: A gente já se viu em algum lugar?
translation.en: Have we met somewhere?

items.label: interrogative particle
items.explanation: か at the end turns the sentence into a question.

items.jp: お名前は何ですか？

translation.pt-BR: Como você se chama?
translation.en: What is your name?

items.label: partícula interrogativa
items.explanation: か no fim transforma a frase em pergunta.

items.jp: 今何時か分かりますか。

translation.pt-BR: Você sabe que horas são?
translation.en: Have you got the time?

items.label: partícula interrogativa
items.explanation: か no fim transforma a frase em pergunta.

items.jp: 何を食べたらいいですか。

translation.pt-BR: O que eu devo comer?
translation.en: What should I eat?

items.label: interrogative particle
items.explanation: か at the end turns the sentence into a question, forming the pattern 〜たらいいですか ('what should I...?').

items.jp: 何がおいしいですか。

translation.pt-BR: O que é gostoso aqui?
translation.en: What do you suggest?

items.label: partícula interrogativa
items.explanation: か no fim transforma a frase em pergunta.

items.jp: 駅はどこですか。

translation.pt-BR: Onde fica a estação?
translation.en: Where is the railroad station?

items.label: partícula interrogativa
items.explanation: か no fim transforma a frase em pergunta.

items.jp: もしもし、来ていますか。

translation.pt-BR: Alô, você está aí?
translation.en: Are you there?

items.label: interrogative particle
items.explanation: か at the end turns the statement into a question ('are you there?').

items.jp: どちらがあなたのギターですか。

translation.pt-BR: Qual é o seu violão?
translation.en: Which is your guitar?

items.label: interrogative particle
items.explanation: か at the end marks the sentence as a question.
tokens: interrogative pronoun / focus of the question

items.jp: トイレはどこですか。

translation.pt-BR: Onde fica o banheiro?
translation.en: Where is the bathroom?

items.label: partícula interrogativa
items.explanation: か no fim transforma a frase em pergunta.

items.jp: ちょっといいですか。

translation.pt-BR: Você tem um minuto?
translation.en: Do you have a minute?

items.label: interrogative particle
items.explanation: Final か turns the sentence into a question: 'is it okay?'. It is what makes ちょっといいですか a request for permission/attention.

items.jp: この長さはどれくらいですか。

translation.pt-BR: Quanto isso tem de comprimento?
translation.en: How long is this?

items.label: interrogative particle
items.explanation: か at the end turns the sentence into a question.

items.jp: この川は何というのですか。

translation.pt-BR: Como se chama este rio?
translation.en: What is the name of this river?

items.label: interrogative particle
items.explanation: か at the end marks the sentence as a question: 'what is it...?'. It is the standard interrogative marker.
tokens: verb (part of the 何という pattern)

items.jp: いい人みたいじゃないか。

translation.pt-BR: Ele parece ser uma boa pessoa, não acha?
translation.en: He seems like quite a find.

items.label: sentence-final particle of confirmation
items.explanation: Together with じゃない, it forms じゃないか, which here does not really ask: it seeks the listener's agreement ('don't you think?'). That is why it closes the sentence, giving the emphatic/confirming tone.

items.jp: ちょっといいですか？

translation.pt-BR: Posso falar um instante?
translation.en: Can I borrow you for just a minute?

items.label: interrogative particle
items.explanation: か marks the sentence as a question, turning it into the request 'is it okay (if I...)?'.

items.jp: あなたなら、どうしますか？

translation.pt-BR: E você, o que faria?
translation.en: What would you do?

items.label: interrogative particle
items.explanation: か at the end turns the sentence into a polite question; it is the standard question marker in the polite register (with ます).

items.jp: 分けて出してもらえますか。

translation.pt-BR: Você poderia servir separado (em pratos diferentes)?
translation.en: We'd like to split it. Could you bring it to us on two plates?

items.label: interrogative particle
items.explanation: か at the end turns the sentence into a question; combined with もらえますか, it softens the request into 'could you...?'
tokens: main verb of the requested action
auxiliary of request (potential of もらう)

items.jp: それがどこから来たのか分からなかった。

translation.pt-BR: Eu não sabia de onde aquilo tinha vindo.
translation.en: I didn't know where it came from.

items.label: particle of origin/starting point
items.explanation: から after どこ indicates the point from which something comes: 'from where'.

items.jp: テーブルにいすが五つある

translation.pt-BR: Tem cinco cadeiras em volta da mesa.
translation.en: There are five chairs at the table.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks what exists. With existence verbs like ある, the item that is present always takes が, not は.

items.jp: どの店が安いですか

translation.pt-BR: Qual loja é barata?
translation.en: Which store is cheap?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks どの店 as the subject; with an interrogative pronoun/determiner が is used because it is the information one wants to find out.

items.jp: 誰がこの本を読みましたか

translation.pt-BR: Quem leu este livro?
translation.en: Who read this book?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 誰 as the subject of the action; with an interrogative pronoun like 誰, が is mandatory (never は).

items.jp: だって、お金がないんだ

translation.pt-BR: É que eu não tenho dinheiro.
translation.en: But I don't have any money.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marca お金 como o sujeito de ない, isto é, quem faz ou de quem se diz o que o predicado exprime.

items.jp: 大きな鷲が山の上を翔る

translation.pt-BR: Uma águia grande voa por cima da montanha.
translation.en: A big eagle flies over the mountain.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 鷲 as the subject that flies.

items.jp: 入り口がわからない

translation.pt-BR: Não sei onde fica a entrada.
translation.en: I don't know where the entrance is.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 入り口 as that which is understood; the verb わかる requires が, and not を, for what is comprehended.

items.jp: どの人があなたの先生ですか

translation.pt-BR: Qual pessoa é a sua professora?
translation.en: Which person is your teacher?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks どの人 (which person) as the subject. In choice questions with どの, が is the natural particle because we are identifying a specific item within a group.

items.jp: りんごが九つある

translation.pt-BR: Tem nove maçãs.
translation.en: There are nine apples.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks りんご as that which exists; with the verb of existence ある, it is が (and not は) that points to what is present.

items.jp: 今にも電車が来る

translation.pt-BR: O trem está para chegar a qualquer momento.
translation.en: The train is about to arrive at any moment.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marca 電車 como o sujeito de 来る, isto é, quem faz ou de quem se diz o que o predicado exprime.

items.jp: ところが、だれもいなかった

translation.pt-BR: Só que não tinha ninguém.
translation.en: However, nobody was there.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marca ところ como o sujeito daquilo que se afirma em seguida.

items.jp: りんごが九つあります

translation.pt-BR: Tem nove maçãs.
translation.en: There are nine apples.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks りんご as what exists; with verbs of existence (ある/いる) the counted item usually comes with が.

items.jp: なぜなら、時間がないからだ

translation.pt-BR: Isso porque não tem tempo.
translation.en: That's because there is no time.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marca 時間 como o sujeito de ない, isto é, quem faz ou de quem se diz o que o predicado exprime.

items.jp: テーブルの上にコップが四つあります

translation.pt-BR: Tem quatro copos em cima da mesa.
translation.en: There are four glasses on the table.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks コップ as the subject that exists. In existence sentences with ある/いる, what exists is marked by が.

items.jp: ノートに名前が書いてある

translation.pt-BR: Tem um nome escrito no caderno.
translation.en: There's a name written in the notebook.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 名前 as the thing that is in the resultant state of having been written.
tokens: subject (thing that is in the resulting state)
main verb in the て form

items.jp: かばんの中にペンが五つある

translation.pt-BR: Tem cinco canetas dentro da bolsa.
translation.en: There are five pens inside the bag.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks what exists. With ある, the present item always takes が (ペンが = the pens).

items.jp: フィルムがもうありません

translation.pt-BR: Não tem mais filme.
translation.en: There's no more film.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks フィルム as that whose existence is being denied; with existence verbs (ある/ない) the item is typically marked by が, not は.

items.jp: テーブルにコップが六つあります

translation.pt-BR: Tem seis copos na mesa.
translation.en: There are six glasses on the table.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks コップ as that which exists on the table.

items.jp: マッチがもうない

translation.pt-BR: Já não tem mais fósforo.
translation.en: There are no more matches.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks マッチ as that whose existence is being negated; with existence verbs (ある/ない) the subject is marked by が, not は.

items.jp: もうお金がありません

translation.pt-BR: Já não tenho mais dinheiro.
translation.en: I don't have any money left.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks お金 (money) as the subject of the verb ある (to exist); with verbs of existence が is used, not を.

items.jp: 見せたいところがあるの。

translation.pt-BR: Tem um lugar que eu quero te mostrar.
translation.en: There's a place I'd like to show you.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: marks 見せたいところ as the subject of ある ("there is a place I want to show"); が of subject, not the conjunction ところが.

items.jp: ポーチにスカンクがいます。

translation.pt-BR: Tem um cangambá na varanda.
translation.en: There's a skunk on the porch.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks スカンク as the being that exists in the pattern ～がいます; what exists with いる always takes が.

items.jp: 車があればなあ。

translation.pt-BR: Ah, se eu tivesse um carro...
translation.en: I wish I had a car.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 車 (car) as the subject that 'exists/there is'. With the existential verb ある, が is used for what exists.

items.jp: 日本語の話せるスタッフがいますか。

translation.pt-BR: Vocês têm algum funcionário que fale japonês?
translation.en: Do you have any employees who speak Japanese?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks スタッフ as the being whose existence is asked about (the subject of いる).
tokens: verb of the relative clause (modifies スタッフ)

items.jp: 千人もの人がそこにいた。

translation.pt-BR: Havia nada menos que mil pessoas ali.
translation.en: As many as a thousand people were there.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 人 ('people') as the subject that existed/was present (いた).

items.jp: 車があればどんなによいだろう。

translation.pt-BR: Como seria bom se eu tivesse um carro!
translation.en: How I wish I had a car.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 車 (car) as the subject of the verb ある (to exist/there is): 'there being a car'.

items.jp: 車があればそこへ行ける。

translation.pt-BR: Se eu tiver um carro, dá para ir até lá.
translation.en: We can go there with the help of a car.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 車 ('car') as what exists in the conditional clause (車がある = 'there is a car').

items.jp: 痔があります。

translation.pt-BR: Tenho hemorroidas.
translation.en: I have hemorrhoids.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 痔 as what exists in the pattern ～があります; with ある, what exists always takes が, not は.

items.jp: 時間がありますか。

translation.pt-BR: Você tem um tempo?
translation.en: Do you have some time?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 時間 as what exists in the pattern ～があります; what exists with ある always takes が.

items.jp: 狐がわなにかかった。

translation.pt-BR: A raposa caiu na armadilha.
translation.en: A fox was caught in the snare.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 狐 as the one who undergoes/performs the action: it is the fox that falls into the trap.

items.jp: 何人の子どもがいますか。

translation.pt-BR: Quantos filhos você tem?
translation.en: How many children do you have?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 子ども as that which 'exists'; with the verb いる, the being that exists always takes が.

items.jp: 何がおいしいですか。

translation.pt-BR: O que é gostoso aqui?
translation.en: What do you suggest?

items.label: partícula de sujeito
items.explanation: が marca 何 como o sujeito de おいしい, isto é, quem faz ou de quem se diz o que o predicado exprime.

items.jp: 右足がしびれちゃった。

translation.pt-BR: Meu pé direito ficou dormente.
translation.en: My right foot is sleeping.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 右足 as the subject that underwent the change of state; in descriptions of physical sensations (tingling, pain), が is used to point to the affected body part.

items.jp: ハウスダストにアレルギーがあります。

translation.pt-BR: Ele tem alergia a poeira doméstica.
translation.en: He is allergic to house dust.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks アレルギー as what exists in the pattern ～があります; with ある/いる, what exists is always marked by が.

items.jp: ネコがいる。

translation.pt-BR: Há um gato.
translation.en: There is a cat.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks ネコ as that which exists; living beings that exist take が with いる.

items.jp: どんなワインがありますか。

translation.pt-BR: Que tipos de vinho vocês têm?
translation.en: What kind of wine do you have?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks ワイン as the subject of the existence verb ある; with ある/いる one uses が (not は) to introduce/ask about the existence of something.
tokens: subject (the thing whose existence is asked about)
main verb (existence of an inanimate thing)

items.jp: いすの上にねこがいます。

translation.pt-BR: Tem um gato em cima da cadeira.
translation.en: There is a cat on the chair.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks ねこ as the being that exists (the subject of the existential verb いる).

items.jp: さあ、ピザがいる人ー！

translation.pt-BR: Bem, quem quer pizza?
translation.en: Hey, who wants pizza?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks ピザ as that whose existence/possession is asserted with いる; it is the typical particle of the pattern がいる.
tokens: subject of 要る (the thing needed), marked by が

items.jp: 学校に人がいる。

translation.pt-BR: Há pessoas na escola.
translation.en: There are people at school.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 人 as that which exists; the being that exists with いる is marked by が.

items.jp: 人がいる。

translation.pt-BR: Há pessoas.
translation.en: There are people.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 人 as that which exists; with いる, the being that exists is marked by が.

items.jp: 話があるんだけど。

translation.pt-BR: É que eu queria falar uma coisa com você...
translation.en: Can we talk in private?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 話 as that which 'exists'; with ある, it indicates what there is ('there's a matter').

items.jp: 会ってほしい人がいるんだ。

translation.pt-BR: Tem uma pessoa que eu quero que você conheça.
translation.en: I have someone I want you to meet.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 人 ('the person') as the subject of いる ('to exist'): 'there is a person...'; typical with existence verbs.
tokens: nominal head (modified by the relative clause)

items.jp: いつでも来ていいよ

translation.pt-BR: Pode vir quando quiser.
translation.en: You can come anytime.

items.label: connective particle (て form)
items.explanation: て liga 来る ao que vem depois (いい) e encadeia os dois dentro da mesma frase.

items.jp: どうしても行きたいんです

translation.pt-BR: Eu quero ir de qualquer jeito.
translation.en: I want to go no matter what.

items.label: connective particle (て form)
items.explanation: て liga する ao que vem depois (も) e encadeia os dois dentro da mesma frase.

items.jp: それにしても、おきれいですね。

translation.pt-BR: Mesmo assim, você está linda, hein.
translation.en: By the way, you look really beautiful.

items.label: connective particle (て form)
items.explanation: て liga する ao que vem depois (も) e encadeia os dois dentro da mesma frase.

items.jp: 外に出てもいいですか？

translation.pt-BR: Posso sair (lá para fora)?
translation.en: Can I go outside?

items.label: connective particle (te-form)
items.explanation: The て forms the て-form of 出る, the base needed for 〜てもいい.

items.jp: いてよかった。

translation.pt-BR: Ainda bem que eu estava lá.
translation.en: I was glad I was there.

items.label: connective particle (て form)
items.explanation: This て links the verb いる to the adjective よかった, forming 〜てよかった ('I'm glad [I] was').

items.jp: なでなでしてごらん。

translation.pt-BR: Faz carinho nele.
translation.en: Pet him.

items.label: connective particle (て form)
items.explanation: links the verb して to the auxiliary ごらん, forming the pattern ～てごらん.

items.jp: 電気をつけていただけませんか。

translation.pt-BR: Você poderia acender a luz, por favor?
translation.en: Would you be so kind as to turn the light on?

items.label: connective particle (て form)
items.explanation: て links つける to the auxiliary いただける, forming つけていただける.

items.jp: 出てもいいですか。

translation.pt-BR: Posso sair?
translation.en: May I leave?

items.label: conjunctive particle (て-form)
items.explanation: て puts the verb in the て-form, the obligatory base of the permission pattern 〜てもいい.

items.jp: 先生といってもいろいろある。

translation.pt-BR: Professor é professor, mas tem de tudo.
translation.en: There are teachers and then there are teachers.

items.label: conjunctive particle (te-form)
items.explanation: links いう to the particle も to assemble the concessive phrase ても ("even if / even though").
tokens: verb of the phrase といっても

items.jp: 大学を出てから10年になります。

translation.pt-BR: Já faz dez anos desde que me formei na faculdade.
translation.en: It is ten years since I left college.

items.label: connective particle て
items.explanation: puts 出る into the て-form (出て) to chain with から and form 'after leaving'.
tokens: verb of the first action (in てから)

items.jp: 行ってもよい。

items.explanation: て liga 行く ao que vem depois (も) e encadeia os dois dentro da mesma frase.

translation.en: How did you come to school?

tokens: interrogative adverb (part of どうやって)
lexicalized verb within the expression どうやって

translation.en: Can I eat this?

items.explanation: て puts 食べる in the て-form, the obligatory base of the permission pattern 〜てもいい.

items.explanation: links the verb 見 to the auxiliary ごらん, forming the pattern ～てごらん.

translation.pt-BR: Para julho, hoje está fresco.

items.explanation: Puts びびる in the て-form so it can be followed by なんかない, forming the emphatic negation structure ～てなんかない.
tokens: component of the emphatic なんか

items.jp: 入ってもいいですか？

translation.pt-BR: Posso entrar?
translation.en: Might I come in?

items.label: conjunctive particle (て-form)
items.explanation: て puts 入る in the て-form, the obligatory base of the permission pattern 〜てもいい.

items.jp: どうやってできましたか。

translation.pt-BR: Como isso foi feito?
translation.en: How was this made?

items.label: conjunctive te-form particle (within どうやって)
items.explanation: Integral part of the fixed expression どうやって; the て here makes up the sense of 'in what way'.
tokens: interrogative adverb (part of どうやって)
lexicalized verb within the expression どうやって

items.jp: 話してもいいですか。

translation.pt-BR: Posso falar (com você)?
translation.en: May I speak to you?

items.explanation: Connects the verb 話す to the following structure; it is the 'て' that forms 話して and allows も + いい to be attached.

translation.en: We'd like to split it. Could you bring it to us on two plates?

items.label: connective (links verbs)
items.explanation: It is the connective て that joins 分ける to the next verb, indicating actions in sequence: 'to divide and then...'
tokens: main verb of the requested action
auxiliary of request (potential of もらう)

items.jp: 分けて出してもらえますか。

translation.pt-BR: Você poderia servir separado (em pratos diferentes)?
translation.en: We'd like to split it. Could you bring it to us on two plates?

items.label: connective (links verb to auxiliary)
items.explanation: Links 出す to the auxiliary もらえる, forming the request pattern 〜てもらえる ('to do [something] for me').
tokens: main verb of the requested action
auxiliary of request (potential of もらう)

items.jp: 手を見せてごらん。

translation.pt-BR: Mostra as mãos.
translation.en: Show me your hands.

items.label: connective particle (て form)
items.explanation: links the verb 見せ to the auxiliary ごらん, forming the pattern ～てごらん.

items.jp: ここで会えてよかった。

translation.pt-BR: Que bom poder te encontrar aqui.
translation.en: I'm glad to see you here.

items.label: 〜て connector linking the verb to よかった
items.explanation: Puts 会える in 〜て form (会えて), the mandatory fit for the pattern 〜てよかった to express the satisfaction 'I'm glad that...'.

items.jp: なんで来なかったの？

translation.pt-BR: Por que você não veio?
translation.en: Why didn't you come?

items.label: で que compõe なんで ('por quê')
items.explanation: で se junta a なん e forma なんで: pergunta o motivo, o 'por quê' do dia a dia.

items.jp: この店でパンを買います

translation.pt-BR: Compro pão nesta loja.
translation.en: I buy bread at this store.

items.label: particle of place of action
items.explanation: で marks 店 (shop) as the place where the action of buying takes place; that is why we use で and not に.

items.jp: 学校の入り口で会おう

translation.pt-BR: Vamos nos encontrar na entrada da escola.
translation.en: Let's meet at the school entrance.

items.label: particle of place of action
items.explanation: で marks the place where the meeting will happen: at the entrance.

items.jp: いつでも来ていいよ

translation.pt-BR: Pode vir quando quiser.
translation.en: You can come anytime.

items.label: で que compõe いつでも ('a qualquer hora')
items.explanation: で se apoia em いつ e, com o も seguinte, monta いつでも: qualquer momento serve.

items.jp: 店で飴を二つ買った

translation.pt-BR: Comprei duas balas na loja.
translation.en: I bought two candies at the store.

items.label: location of the action
items.explanation: で marks the place where an active action happens; here, the buying is done 店で (at the shop).

items.jp: どこかで会いましたか

translation.pt-BR: A gente já se viu em algum lugar?
translation.en: Have we met somewhere?

items.label: particle of place of action
items.explanation: で marca どこか como o lugar em que o encontro teria acontecido.

items.jp: 二人っきりで話したいな。

translation.pt-BR: Queria conversar só nós dois.
translation.en: I want to talk to you alone.

items.label: particle of place of action
items.explanation: Este で marca 二人っきり como a condição em que a conversa aconteceria: a sós.

items.jp: でもなんで？

translation.pt-BR: Mas por quê?
translation.en: But why?

items.label: forms the interrogative expression なんで ('why')
items.explanation: This で closes なんで ('why'). Historically it is the 'by means of' particle, but in なんで it has already merged into a single word meaning 'for what reason'.

items.jp: しかしなんでまたこんなところに来たんだ？

translation.pt-BR: Mas por que você veio de novo a um lugar destes?
translation.en: But why did you come to a place like this again?

items.label: particle forming 'why' (なんで)
items.explanation: で together with なん forms なんで ('why'). Here で indicates cause/reason linked to the interrogative なん, asking the reason.
tokens: demonstrative adjective (連体詞, modifies ところ)

items.jp: デパートで来年のカレンダーを買いました。

translation.pt-BR: Comprei um calendário do ano que vem na loja de departamentos.
translation.en: I bought a calendar for next year at the store.

items.label: particle of place of action
items.explanation: で marks デパート as the place where the action of buying happens (で indicates where something is done, unlike に, which indicates where something is).

items.jp: ありがとう。これでけっこうです。

translation.pt-BR: Obrigado. Assim está bom.
translation.en: Thank you. This is fine as it is.

items.label: particle of means/manner ('with this', 'in this way')
items.explanation: で marks これ as the means or situation by which something is settled: これで = 'with this / this way'. It indicates that, given this state of affairs, it is already good enough.

items.jp: 何でもけっこうです。

translation.pt-BR: Qualquer coisa está bom.
translation.en: Anything will do.

items.label: particle that, with 何, forms 'any'
items.explanation: で here is part of the combination でも linked to 何. On its own it would be the particle of means/place, but together with も it forms the expression 何でも.

items.jp: 何で学校に行かないといけないの？

translation.pt-BR: Por que eu preciso ir à escola?
translation.en: Why should I go to school?

items.label: particle forming the interrogative expression 'why'
items.explanation: Together with 何, the particle で forms 何で ('why'), asking the reason for the action.

items.jp: 後でやって。

translation.pt-BR: Faz isso depois.
translation.en: Do it later.

items.label: particle forming the temporal expression 後で
items.explanation: で links to 後 to indicate the moment of the action ('later'); 後で is the fixed unit that situates when to do it.
tokens: adverb of time (head of 後で)

items.jp: なんで聞くの？

translation.pt-BR: Por que você pergunta?
translation.en: Why do you ask?

items.label: forms the interrogative expression なんで ('why')
items.explanation: This で closes なんで ('why'). Together with なん it forms a single interrogative word that indicates the cause/reason of the action.

items.jp: ところで、午後は空いてる？

translation.pt-BR: A propósito, você tá livre à tarde?

items.label: で fossilizado em ところで (mudança de assunto)
items.explanation: で aparece dentro de ところで, o 'a propósito' que introduz o assunto novo. Aqui ele não tem função de lugar.

items.jp: あれ？何だろ？パフォーマンスでもやってるのか？

translation.pt-BR: Hã? O que é isso? Será que estão fazendo uma apresentação de rua ou algo assim?
translation.en: Hello, what's that? Somebody doing street theatre or something?

items.label: forms, together with も, the exemplifying expression でも
items.explanation: This 「で」 is the base that, added to 「も」, forms 「でも」. Here it marks neither place nor means; it is the first half of the construction 「でも」 that gives the sense of 'or something like that'.

items.jp: なんで？

translation.pt-BR: Por quê?
translation.en: Why?

items.label: particle で that, together with なん, forms the interrogative なんで ('why')
items.explanation: で here indicates cause/reason and merges with なん to create なんで, the casual form of 'why'. Although で originally marks means or cause, in なんで the whole is read as a single colloquial interrogative word.

items.jp: 後で話そうね。

translation.pt-BR: A gente conversa depois, tá?
translation.en: We'll talk afterwards.

items.label: marks the point/moment in time
items.explanation: Here で joins 後 to form the phrase 後で ("later"); it indicates the moment when the action will happen.

items.jp: ところで、この後何するの？

translation.pt-BR: A propósito, o que você vai fazer depois?
translation.en: By the way, what are you doing after this?

items.label: で fossilizado em ところで (mudança de assunto)
items.explanation: で faz parte de ところで, o bloco fixo que abre a frase mudando de assunto. Vale como unidade, não como partícula de lugar.

items.label: topic particle
items.explanation: は apresenta 中 como o tópico da frase, ou seja, o assunto sobre o qual se faz a afirmação seguinte.

items.explanation: は apresenta お名前 como o tópico da frase, ou seja, o assunto sobre o qual se faz a afirmação seguinte.

items.label: partícula de tópico
items.explanation: は apresenta 駅 como o tópico da frase, ou seja, o assunto sobre o qual se faz a afirmação seguinte.

items.jp: トイレはどこですか。

translation.pt-BR: Onde fica o banheiro?

items.label: partícula de tópico
items.explanation: は apresenta トイレ como o tópico da frase, ou seja, o assunto sobre o qual se faz a afirmação seguinte.

items.jp: この長さはどれくらいですか。

items.explanation: は apresenta この長さ como o tópico da frase, ou seja, o assunto sobre o qual se faz a afirmação seguinte.

items.jp: ところで、午後は空いてる？

translation.pt-BR: A propósito, você tá livre à tarde?
translation.en: By the way, are you free this afternoon?

items.label: topic particle
items.explanation: は apresenta 午後 como o tópico da frase, ou seja, o assunto sobre o qual se faz a afirmação seguinte.

items.jp: 今にも電車が来る

items.explanation: も fecha 今に e completa 今にも: o trem está a ponto de chegar, a qualquer segundo.

translation.pt-BR: Você vai? Ou não vai?
translation.en: Are you going? Or not?

items.label: も que compõe o conector それとも ('ou então')
items.explanation: も fecha それと e completa それとも: apresenta a segunda opção, 'ou então'.

items.jp: いつでも来ていいよ

translation.pt-BR: Pode vir quando quiser.
translation.en: You can come anytime.

items.label: も da expressão でも (generalização)
items.explanation: も fecha いつで e completa いつでも: soma todos os horários possíveis.

items.jp: あなたも来ればいいのに。

translation.pt-BR: Você também podia vir.
translation.en: I wish you could come, too.

items.explanation: も marca あなた como mais um na conta: você também, junto com quem já vai.

translation.en: Looks like another nice day.

items.label: partícula de inclusão ('também')
items.explanation: も vem depois de 今日 e soma o dia de hoje aos anteriores: hoje também faz tempo bom.

items.jp: 何でもけっこうです。

translation.pt-BR: Qualquer coisa está bom.
translation.en: Anything will do.

items.label: particle of total inclusion ('also/even'), forming 'any'
items.explanation: も combines with 何で to give 何でも = 'anything, whatever it may be'. It is the interrogative + でも pattern that expresses total scope ('any and all').

items.jp: どうもごりっぱな言いわけだよ。

items.explanation: も is part of the adverbial phrase どうも, reinforcing the tone ("frankly / really").

items.jp: でももヘチマもないわ。

translation.pt-BR: Nada de 'mas'!
translation.en: There's no but about it!

items.label: particle も (inclusion 'neither... nor')
items.explanation: Here も marks each item in the enumeration that will be negated by ない: 'there is neither this nor that'. Repeated in 'X も Y も + negation' it creates the structure 'neither X nor Y'.

items.jp: あれ？何だろ？パフォーマンスでもやってるのか？

translation.en: Hello, what's that? Somebody doing street theatre or something?

items.label: closes the expression でも ('or something like that')
items.explanation: 「も」 here joins 「で」 to create 「でも」, which after a noun means 'or something like that', giving a vague, noncommittal tone to the speaker's guess.

items.jp: 今に分かるよ

translation.pt-BR: Logo você vai entender.

items.explanation: よ no fim passa a informação ao ouvinte com ênfase, como quem diz 'olha' ou 'viu'.

items.jp: いつでも来ていいよ

translation.pt-BR: Isso aí eu vou perguntar.
translation.en: I will ask that.

items.label: emphatic final particle
items.explanation: よ asserts the speaker's intention to the listener ('leave it to me, I'll ask').

items.jp: テレビ見とくよ。

items.label: emphatic final particle
items.explanation: よ at the end asserts the speaker's intention ('leave it to me', 'you'll see'), in an informal and assertive tone.

items.jp: どうもごりっぱな言いわけだよ。

translation.pt-BR: Nossa, que desculpa esfarrapada.
translation.en: That is a fine excuse.

items.label: emphatic final particle
items.explanation: よ at the end adds emphasis and a tone of one who comments/criticizes, addressing the listener.

items.jp: もうやっちゃったよ。

translation.pt-BR: Já fiz isso.
translation.en: I've already done it.

items.label: emphatic final particle
items.explanation: よ informs the listener of something they perhaps did not know ('I already did it, you know'); it gives firmness and closes the sentence with a tone of notice/assurance.

items.jp: 今じゃないんだとしたら、いつなのよ？

translation.pt-BR: Se não for agora, então quando?

items.label: emphatic final particle

items.label: direct-object marker

items.jp: ははは りょうりを つくるのが じょうずです

items.jp: 子どもに飴をあげた

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marca 計五人 como o sujeito de 来る, isto é, quem faz ou de quem se diz o que o predicado exprime.

items.jp: 車より自転車のほうが安い

translation.pt-BR: A bicicleta é mais barata que o carro.
translation.en: A bicycle is cheaper than a car.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 自転車のほう as the subject of 安い: it is the bicycle side that is cheap.
tokens: supporting noun (ほう, marks the preferred alternative)

items.jp: あなたがいると安心する

translation.pt-BR: Quando você está por perto, eu fico tranquilo.
translation.en: When you're around, I feel at ease.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks あなた as the subject of いる; within a subordinate/conditional clause the subject usually takes が, not は.
tokens: nominal head of the compound verb

items.jp: あなたは兄弟がいますか

translation.pt-BR: Você tem irmãos?
translation.en: Do you have any siblings?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 兄弟 as that whose existence is being questioned; with います, what one possesses takes が.

items.jp: このカレンダーには写真があります

translation.pt-BR: Neste calendário tem fotos.
translation.en: This calendar has photos.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 「写真」as that whose existence is asserted with あります.

items.jp: このズボンはポケットが大きい

translation.pt-BR: Esta calça tem bolsos grandes.
translation.en: These pants have big pockets.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks ポケット as the subject of the adjective 大きい: it is the pocket that is big, within the topic 'trousers'. It forms the 〜は〜が pattern.

items.jp: 車がないと買い物が不便です

translation.pt-BR: Se você não tem carro, fazer compras é um perrengue.
translation.en: If you don't have a car, shopping is a hassle.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 車 as the subject of ない; with existence verbs/adjectives (ある/ない), what exists or is lacking takes が.

items.jp: 車がないと買い物が不便です

translation.pt-BR: Se você não tem carro, fazer compras é um perrengue.
translation.en: If you don't have a car, shopping is a hassle.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 買い物 (shopping) as the subject of the predicate 不便です (that which becomes inconvenient).

items.jp: 日曜日に市が立つ

translation.pt-BR: Aos domingos tem feira.
translation.en: A market is held on Sunday.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marca 市 como o sujeito de 立つ, isto é, quem faz ou de quem se diz o que o predicado exprime.

items.jp: 南の空が明るいです

translation.pt-BR: O céu ao sul está claro.
translation.en: The sky to the south is bright.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 空 as the subject whose quality (being clear) is being described.

items.jp: 山の上から海が見られる

translation.pt-BR: Do alto da montanha dá pra ver o mar.
translation.en: From the top of the mountain you can see the sea.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 海 as the grammatical subject of the potential verb 見られる: it is the sea that 'can be seen'.

items.jp: コーヒーよりお茶のほうがいい

translation.pt-BR: Prefiro chá a café.
translation.en: I prefer tea to coffee.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks お茶のほう as the subject of いい: it is the tea side that is the better one.
tokens: supporting noun (ほう, marks the preferred alternative)

items.jp: 校長が朝の話をしました

translation.pt-BR: O diretor deu o aviso da manhã.
translation.en: The principal gave the morning announcements.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が points to 校長 (principal) as who carries out the action of speaking; with が the subject is presented neutrally, as new information.

items.jp: 今日より明日のほうが暑い

translation.pt-BR: Amanhã vai estar mais quente do que hoje.
translation.en: Tomorrow will be hotter than today.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 明日のほう as the subject of 暑い: it is the tomorrow side that is hotter.
tokens: supporting noun (ほう, marks the preferred alternative)

items.jp: 新しい産業が町を元気にしました

translation.pt-BR: A nova indústria deu vida nova à cidade.
translation.en: The new industry brought new life to the town.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 産業 as the subject that performs the action, that is, who 'gave life' to the town. が (and not は) is used because the industry is presented as new information, the agent of the transformation.

items.jp: 駅の前に自転車がたくさんある

translation.pt-BR: Tem muitas bicicletas na frente da estação.
translation.en: There are a lot of bikes in front of the station.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 自転車 as what exists. In sentences with ある/いる, it is が (not は) that presents what is present in the place.

items.jp: だれが来るか教えてください

translation.pt-BR: Me diga quem vem, por favor.
translation.en: Please tell me who's coming.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks だれ as the subject of 来る; with interrogative pronouns like だれ one uses が, never は.
tokens: interrogative pronoun (core of the embedded question)

items.jp: どの色がいいですか

translation.pt-BR: Qual cor você prefere?
translation.en: Which color do you prefer?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 色 (color) as the subject being asked about. In questions with どの we use が (and not は) because we are choosing an item within a set, not commenting on an already-known topic.

items.jp: 駅が遠くて、とても不便です

translation.pt-BR: A estação fica longe, então é bem inconveniente.
translation.en: The station is far away and quite inconvenient.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 駅 as the subject that has the characteristic of being far; が is used to introduce/highlight the subject of a situation.

items.jp: 時間がないので急ぎましょう

translation.pt-BR: Não temos tempo, então vamos nos apressar.
translation.en: We don't have time, so let's hurry.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 時間 as that whose existence is denied (with ない); it is the standard use of が with ある/ない.
tokens: predicate (i-adjective ない, negation of ある)

items.jp: 思わず大きな声が出た

translation.pt-BR: Sem querer, saiu um grito.
translation.en: A loud voice came out of me without my meaning it.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marca 大きな声 como o sujeito de 出る, isto é, quem faz ou de quem se diz o que o predicado exprime.

items.jp: この服が気に入りました

translation.pt-BR: Eu gostei dessa roupa.
translation.en: I took a liking to these clothes.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marca この服 como o sujeito de 入る, isto é, quem faz ou de quem se diz o que o predicado exprime.

items.jp: 鳥が空を翔る

translation.pt-BR: O pássaro voa pelo céu.
translation.en: The bird flies through the sky.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 鳥 as the subject that performs the action of flying.

items.jp: 車が三台止まっている

translation.pt-BR: Tem três carros estacionados.
translation.en: There are three cars parked.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が introduces 車 ('car') as the subject appearing in the scene; it is typical for が to introduce something new or observed to exist.
tokens: numeral (part of the count 三台)

items.jp: もしお金があれば旅行したい

translation.pt-BR: Se eu tivesse dinheiro, gostaria de viajar.
translation.en: If I had money, I'd like to travel.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks お金 as what 'exists/there is' with ある; with existence verbs が is used, not を.
tokens: object / base of the compound verb

items.jp: 電車のドアがすっと開きました

translation.pt-BR: A porta do trem se abriu suavemente.
translation.en: The train door opened smoothly.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 電車のドア as the subject that performs the action of opening.

items.jp: 白い鳥が海の上を翔る

translation.pt-BR: Um pássaro branco voa por cima do mar.
translation.en: A white bird flies over the sea.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 鳥 as the subject that flies.

items.jp: この町はバスが少なくて不便だ

translation.pt-BR: Esta cidade tem poucos ônibus, então é inconveniente.
translation.en: This town has few buses, so it's inconvenient.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks バス (bus) as the internal subject of the adjective 少ない; within a topic marked by は, it is common for the specific subject to take が.

items.jp: 食料品がもうない

translation.pt-BR: Os mantimentos já acabaram.
translation.en: The groceries have already run out.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: 'が' marks 食料品 as the thing whose existence is being negated: it is what 'there is no longer'.

items.jp: 犬が外に出たがる

translation.pt-BR: O cachorro quer sair (fica querendo ir pra fora).
translation.en: The dog wants to go out (keeps wanting to go outside).

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 犬 as the one who feels/shows the desire, the subject of 出たがる.

items.jp: 研究室のドアが開いている

translation.pt-BR: A porta do laboratório de pesquisa está aberta.
translation.en: The door to the research lab is open.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks ドア as the subject in the described state; with state/change verbs like 開いている, が is used, not は, to present the information as a neutral observation.

items.jp: あの人が新しい校長です

translation.pt-BR: Aquela pessoa é o novo diretor.
translation.en: That person is the new principal.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks あの人 as the subject with a nuance of identification ('it is that person who...'), distinguishing them from the others as the new principal.

items.jp: しまった、時間がない

translation.pt-BR: Droga, não tem tempo.
translation.en: Oh no, there's no time.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marca 時間 como o sujeito de ない, isto é, quem faz ou de quem se diz o que o predicado exprime.

items.jp: 急に人が多くなった

translation.pt-BR: De repente ficou cheio de gente.
translation.en: Suddenly there were a lot of people.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marca 人 como o sujeito de 多い, isto é, quem faz ou de quem se diz o que o predicado exprime.

items.jp: 先生が教室に入ってきた

translation.pt-BR: O professor entrou na sala de aula.
translation.en: The teacher came into the classroom.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が presents 先生 as the subject who performs the action, marking it as new information (it was the teacher who entered).

items.jp: お金があったら旅行したい

translation.pt-BR: Se eu tivesse dinheiro, queria viajar.
translation.en: If I had money, I'd want to travel.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks お金 ('money') as the subject of the existence verb ある; with ある/いる what exists is presented with が (お金がある = to have/there to be money).
tokens: object (forms the verb 旅行する)

items.jp: ラジカセのおとが小さい

translation.pt-BR: O som do rádio-gravador está baixo.
translation.en: The boombox's volume is low.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks おと as that which is 'low'; が (and not は) is used because the sentence merely describes/states a characteristic of the sound, without highlighting it as an already-established topic.

items.jp: ４月の１日に学校が始まる

translation.pt-BR: No dia primeiro de abril, as aulas começam.
translation.en: Classes start on the first of April.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 学校 as the subject undergoing the intransitive action 始まる. With verbs that 'happen on their own', が is used (not を) to point to what begins.

items.jp: 電車が止まっているんです

translation.pt-BR: É que o trem está parado.
translation.en: It's because the train is stopped.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 電車 (train) as the subject that is stopped; it describes a fact about it.

items.jp: もし時間があったら電話してください

translation.pt-BR: Se você tiver tempo, me liga, por favor.
translation.en: If you have time, please give me a call.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 時間 as what 'exists/there is' with ある; existence verbs require が.
tokens: object / base of the compound verb

items.jp: 近くにガソリンスタンドがありますか

translation.pt-BR: Tem algum posto de gasolina aqui perto?
translation.en: Is there a gas station near here?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks ガソリンスタンド as the subject that exists; with ある/あります, が is used.

items.jp: 行きたいけれど、時間がない

translation.pt-BR: Eu queria ir, mas não tenho tempo.
translation.en: I want to go, but I don't have time.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 時間 as the subject whose existence is negated by ない; with ある/ない, が is used, not を.

items.jp: 質問が一つあります

translation.pt-BR: Eu tenho uma pergunta.
translation.en: I have a question.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 質問 as what exists. With the existence verb ある/あります, the thing that exists is marked by が.

items.jp: 今月の電気代が高かった

translation.pt-BR: A conta de luz deste mês veio cara.
translation.en: This month's electricity bill came out high.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 電気代 as the subject that takes on the quality described by 高かった ('was expensive').

items.jp: 今日は仕事が休みなんです

translation.pt-BR: É que hoje eu estou de folga no trabalho.
translation.en: It's because I have the day off work today.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 仕事 (work) as what 'is off'; here it indicates the subject of the situation described.
tokens: auxiliary (copula だ in the な form)

items.jp: 教室にいすが九つある

translation.pt-BR: Tem nove cadeiras na sala de aula.
translation.en: There are nine chairs in the classroom.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks いす as what exists in the room; the counted item comes with が together with ある.

items.jp: 二人が会話をする

translation.pt-BR: Os dois conversam.
translation.en: Two of them have a conversation.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 二人 (the two) as the subject that performs the action. Here it presents a concrete fact about who acts.

items.jp: 多くの学生が、アルバイトをします

translation.pt-BR: Muitos estudantes trabalham meio período.
translation.en: Many students have part-time jobs.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 多くの学生 as the subject that performs the action of working part-time.

items.jp: 人には二つタイプが有ります

translation.pt-BR: Existem dois tipos de pessoa.
translation.en: There are two types of people.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks タイプ as that which exists. In sentences with ある/いる, the thing that exists always takes が.

items.jp: 色々な人がこのブログを見ているようです

translation.pt-BR: Parece que vários tipos de pessoas estão lendo este blog.
translation.en: It seems that various kinds of people are reading this blog.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 色々な人 as the subject performing the action of 見ている; one uses が (and not は) because the information is new/descriptive, presenting who is reading.

items.jp: 世界中で多くの研究が行われた

translation.pt-BR: Muitas pesquisas foram realizadas pelo mundo todo.
translation.en: A lot of research was conducted all around the world.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 研究 as the grammatical subject of the passive verb 行われた (that which was carried out).

items.jp: あいつ、ほんと口が軽いからな。

translation.pt-BR: É que aquele cara tem a língua bem solta, né.
translation.en: He's a real blabbermouth.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 口 ('mouth') as the subject of 軽い; together they form the idiom 口が軽い ('to be indiscreet/loose-lipped').
tokens: subject (within the idiom 口が軽い)

items.jp: 学校が終わってから何してる？

translation.pt-BR: O que você faz depois da escola?
translation.en: What do you do after school?

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 学校 as the subject of the verb 終わる within the clause 学校が終わって ('the school ends').
tokens: verb of the first action (てから)

items.jp: そんな映画見るわけがない！

translation.pt-BR: Não tem como eu assistir a um filme desses!
translation.en: There's no way I'd watch that kind of movie.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks わけ as the subject of ない, forming the fixed expression わけがない that categorically denies the possibility.
tokens: main verb (clause that takes わけがない)
formal noun of the わけがない pattern
negative predicate (adjective ない, 'to not exist')

items.jp: やりたいことがあるの。

translation.pt-BR: Tem coisas que eu quero fazer.
translation.en: There are things I want to do.

items.label: subject particle
items.explanation: が marks 'やりたいこと' (the things I want to do) as that which exists; with the verb ある, what exists is always marked by が, not by を.
